star_forts.name: Fort Monroe (Old Point Comfort)
star_forts.description: Massive six-bastioned stone and brick star fort surrounded by a saltwater moat. The largest stone fort ever built in the United States, covering 565 acres. Official construction claims 1819–1834 with over 40 million bricks and granite revetments.

star_forts.name: Castillo de San Marcos
star_forts.description: Oldest masonry fortification in the continental US. Four-pointed diamond star citadel constructed with coquina stone (quarried shell-stone). Features complex bastion angles and cannon emplacements.

star_forts.name: Fort Jefferson (Dry Tortugas)
star_forts.description: Unbelievable remote maritime bastion citadel containing over 16 million handmade bricks situated 70 miles west of Key West on an isolated sand key. Massive hexagonal bastions and tiered casemates.

star_forts.name: Fort Bourtange
star_forts.description: Geometrically pristine five-pointed star village and fortress in the Netherlands, complete with concentric perimeter moats, ravelins, counterguards, and star earthworks.

star_forts.name: Palmanova Fortress City
star_forts.description: Ideal 9-pointed concentric star city with radial streets converging on a central hexagonal piazza. Built with colossal earthen ramparts, stone revetments, and moats.

star_forts.name: Neuf-Brisach Octagonal Citadel
star_forts.description: Perfect octagonal star city fortification designed by Vauban on the Rhine border, featuring double concentric curtain walls, ravelins, and monumental stone gate portals.

star_forts.name: Goryōkaku Star Fort
star_forts.description: Extremely rare 5-pointed Western-style star fort located in Hakodate, Japan, surrounded by a water-filled moat and stone-faced earthen ramparts.

star_forts.name: Fort McHenry Star Bastion
star_forts.description: Pentagonal bastion star fort defending Baltimore Harbor. Features brick curtain walls, pentagonal corners, and dry moat ditches with underground magazines.

train_stations.name: Grand Central Terminal
train_stations.description: Monumental Beaux-Arts palace covering 48 acres across subterranean levels. Features celestial ceiling murals, monumental carved statuary of Mercury and Minerva, and immense granite columns.

train_stations.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (Victoria Terminus)
train_stations.description: High Victorian Gothic cathedral-station combining Italianate and Indian stone carving. Features a massive ribbed stone dome, gargoyles, stained glass, and intricate marble vaulting.

train_stations.name: St Pancras International
train_stations.description: Gothic Revival palace designed by George Gilbert Scott featuring the Barlow train shed, which at the time of construction was the largest single-span roof in the world. Red brick clock tower and intricate stone tracery.

train_stations.name: Antwerpen-Centraal Station
train_stations.description: Widely known as the 'Railway Cathedral'. Eclectic monumental stone terminal with a 75-meter high dome, monumental grand staircase, marble clad hallways, and iron vaulted train shed.

train_stations.name: Milano Centrale
train_stations.description: Colossal limestone terminal spanning 200 meters across. Features Art Nouveau, Beaux-Arts, and Classical Roman motifs with massive winged Pegasus sculptures and soaring stone vaults.

train_stations.name: Dunedin Railway Station
train_stations.description: Flemish Renaissance stone palace built with dark Kokonga basalt and Oamaru limestone trim. Features Royal Doulton porcelain mosaic floors with nearly 750,000 tiles and stained glass windows.

carnegie.name: Carnegie Library of Pittsburgh (Main)
carnegie.description: Flagship Carnegie Library and Institute. Monumental Italian Renaissance sandstone complex designed by Longfellow, Alden & Harlow, featuring Corinthian colonnades and barrel-vaulted marble halls.

carnegie.name: Carnegie Library of Washington D.C.
carnegie.description: Beaux-Arts classical white marble palace located at Mount Vernon Square. Designed by Ackerman & Ross with monumental rusticated arched entrances and carved stone balustrades.

carnegie.name: West Tampa Carnegie Free Library
carnegie.description: Classical Revival brick and stone library at 2312 W. Union Street in Tampa. Monumental Ionic columns, elevated masonry foundation, and ornate dental cornices.

carnegie.name: Denver Carnegie Public Library (McNichols)
carnegie.description: Grand Greek Revival limestone temple in Denver Civic Center. Features massive fluted Ionic columns, stone pilasters, and soaring ceilings.

carnegie.name: Louisville Free Public Library (Main)
carnegie.description: Beaux-Arts limestone landmark covering an entire city block. Features grand Corinthian porticoes, stained glass rotunda domes, and monumental marble staircases.
